free_string.message: Sorting Arm X motor will out of limit
free_string.trigger: aSortArm.cpp:677 MoveSortArmX(): if(HSys.Mot.MSortingArmX->CheckSoftLimit(Position)==false) -> raise at aSortArm.cpp:679 ShowMotorLimitError("WAR0154","Sorting Arm X motor will out of limit", HSys.Mot.MSortingArmX->SoftLimitDetail(Position)). CheckSoftLimit is a pure numeric compare: return (p<=Motor->SoftLimitP && p>=Motor->SoftLimitN) at MyMotor.cpp:506. This is a PRE-MOVE software soft-limit guard, not a physical limit-switch trip; it fires before the motor is commanded, when the requested X target falls outside the configured band. SoftLimitDetail (MyMotor.cpp:512-516) prints the numeric line 'target=%d  now=%d  soft limit N=%d ~ P=%d  (unit:1/100mm)'. VERIFIED sole WAR0154 raise site (grep: only aSortArm.cpp:679). The XY pre-check at aSortArm.cpp:2250 runs the same CheckSoftLimit but returns Err="Sorting Arm X target over soft limit" instead of raising this code.
root_causes: A SortArm X destination teach value (e.g. an Auto/Loader sort-column X, or a Pitch X target) is set beyond the configured soft-limit band [SoftLimitN, SoftLimitP].

Computed cell/slot X target (GetSortArmCellX from base X + column/pitch, aSortArm.cpp:2248) overshoots the physical range for a given tray geometry or column index; this XPosition flows into MoveSortArmX (aSortArm.cpp:810/819/2319).
SoftLimitN/SoftLimitP in the motor table for MSortingArmX configured too tight to cover the required travel.
Arm home/origin offset shifted from lost steps or a bad home, so 'now' is out of calibration and an otherwise-valid target resolves outside the band.

The SortArm teach-advanced test path (uteach case 30 -> MoveSuckerToCell -> MoveSortArmX, aSortArm.cpp:2319; see uteach.cpp:1421) commanded an X target outside the band and re-raised WAR0154. NOTE: the generic Motor Test / Teach jog (uMotorTest.cpp:2560 / uteach.cpp:870) uses the SAME CheckSoftLimit guard but raises its own per-motor over-limit code, NOT WAR0154.

error_types.label: Power Off
error_types.meaning: Servo drive is de-energized: the A6 amp asserts ALM while holding INP (in-position, no command in flight) and the card servo-alarm status bit is also set. Interpreted as 'servo power lost'. Classifier branch GetErrorIndex()==0 (MyMotor.cpp:734-735); code = 50000+index*10+0.
error_types.signal_source: Led[iAlarmLed]=MotDI bit 0x80 (A6 driver ALM, sampled only when ServoAlarmOn) AND Led[iServoalarmLed]=MC88X1PGetMotionInput bit 0x10 (card servo-alarm) AND Led[iInposLed]=MotDI bit 0x40 (A6 INP). Root physical: servo power relay SwMotorRelay / SnMotorPower.
error_types.expected: Drive energized: SwMotorRelay ON, SnMotorPower present; ALM=0, servo-alarm status=0. In the Motor status grid the Alarm/ServoAlarm LEDs are dark.
error_types.actual: ALM(0x80)+servo-alarm(0x10)+INP(0x40) all ON simultaneously = amp powered down / SRV-ON dropped while axis idle.
error_types.check_where: IOsetview (SwMotorRelay output / SnMotorPower input) plus the main Motor status grid (Alarm / ServoAlarm / InPos LEDs for that axis).
error_types.engineer_action: Restore servo/main power; a latched OT/servo alarm is NOT software-clearable (MC88X1 SetServoOn is a no-op), so do a SwMotorRelay Off->On power-cycle, then re-HOME the axis. HOME deliberately cuts and restores motor power and owns this recovery (uHome ProcessMotorHome case 20).

error_types.label: Out Of Torque
error_types.meaning: Drive tripped its alarm while a move was still in progress (INP not yet reached) - the axis could not reach/hold the commanded position: over-torque, overload, or a following stall. Classifier branch GetErrorIndex()==1 (MyMotor.cpp:736-737); code = 50000+index*10+1.
error_types.signal_source: Led[iAlarmLed]=MotDI 0x80 (A6 ALM) AND Led[iServoalarmLed]=MotionInput 0x10 (card servo-alarm), with Led[iInposLed]=MotDI 0x40 OFF (not in position).
error_types.expected: No ALM; INP asserts at the end of each PTP move; commanded NowPos and Encoder converge within the following-error tolerance.
error_types.actual: ALM+servo-alarm set while INP is still 0 -> axis stalled under load / exceeded torque limit mid-move; encoder lags command.
error_types.check_where: MotionView (command NowPos vs Encoder following gap for the stalled axis) plus the Motor status grid (Alarm+ServoAlarm ON, InPos OFF).
error_types.engineer_action: Clear the mechanical binding/overload on that axis, verify the A6 torque limit and load/gear, clear the driver alarm via a SwMotorRelay power-cycle, then re-HOME.

error_types.label: CW sensor ON
error_types.meaning: Axis is sitting on the CW (+) end hard-limit switch. The lit CW limit also force-sets the Alarm LED (ScanMotorStatus:999-1000). Classifier branch GetErrorIndex()==2 (MyMotor.cpp:738-739); code = 50000+index*10+2.
error_types.signal_source: Led[iCwLed]=MC88X1PGetMotionInput bit 0x04 (+LM / CW hard-limit input); Led[iAlarmLed] is forced true by the lit limit.
error_types.expected: CW/+LM hard-limit input OFF (axis inside its travel band); iCwLed LED dark in IOsetview.
error_types.actual: +LM CW limit input ON -> axis physically pressed against / overran the CW end stop.
error_types.check_where: IOsetview (the CW / +LM limit input LED for that axis) plus MotionView (Now Position at the CW extreme).
error_types.engineer_action: Jog the axis OFF the limit with JogN (away from CW); inspect the +LM switch wiring/mounting and check for mechanical overrun. Note: during HOME an on-limit alarm is treated as expected (csystem.cpp:482-483 continue), so this only stops the machine mid-run.

error_types.label: CCW sensor ON
error_types.meaning: Axis is sitting on the CCW (-) end hard-limit switch; the lit CCW limit force-sets the Alarm LED. Classifier branch GetErrorIndex()==3 (MyMotor.cpp:740-741); code = 50000+index*10+3.
error_types.signal_source: Led[iCcwLed]=MC88X1PGetMotionInput bit 0x08 (-LM / CCW hard-limit input); Led[iAlarmLed] forced true by the lit limit.
error_types.expected: CCW/-LM hard-limit input OFF (axis inside travel); iCcwLed LED dark.
error_types.actual: -LM CCW limit input ON -> axis pressed against / overran the CCW end stop.
error_types.check_where: IOsetview (the CCW / -LM limit input LED for that axis) plus MotionView (Now Position at the CCW extreme).
error_types.engineer_action: Jog the axis OFF the limit with JogP (away from CCW); inspect the -LM switch and mechanical overrun. On-limit during HOME is expected (continue); this only halts mid-run.

error_types.label: Soft P position
error_types.meaning: The card software +comp-limit tripped: command position reached/exceeded the configured positive soft limit SoftLimitP. Classifier branch GetErrorIndex()==4 (MyMotor.cpp:742-743); code = 50000+index*10+4.
error_types.signal_source: Led[iSoftcwLed]=MC88X1PGetMotionInput bit 0x01 (card soft/comp CW limit, set from SoftLimitP via SetMC88X1SoftLimit) AND Led[iAlarmLed].
error_types.expected: Now Position within [SoftLimitN, SoftLimitP]; soft-CW flag off.
error_types.actual: Position at/beyond SoftLimitP -> card positive comp-limit asserted.
error_types.check_where: MotionView (Now Position vs the axis SoftLimitP value).
error_types.engineer_action: Jog the axis back inside the soft-limit band; verify teach targets and the SoftLimitP config for that axis; re-HOME if the position reference was lost.

error_types.label: Soft N position
error_types.meaning: The card software -comp-limit tripped: command position reached/fell below the configured negative soft limit SoftLimitN. Classifier branch GetErrorIndex()==5 (MyMotor.cpp:744-745); code = 50000+index*10+5.
error_types.signal_source: Led[iSoftccwLed]=MC88X1PGetMotionInput bit 0x02 (card soft/comp CCW limit, set from SoftLimitN) AND Led[iAlarmLed].
error_types.expected: Now Position within [SoftLimitN, SoftLimitP]; soft-CCW flag off.
error_types.actual: Position at/below SoftLimitN -> card negative comp-limit asserted.
error_types.check_where: MotionView (Now Position vs the axis SoftLimitN value).
error_types.engineer_action: Jog the axis back inside the soft-limit band; verify teach targets and the SoftLimitN config; re-HOME if the position reference is wrong.

error_types.label: position Error / home+restart
error_types.meaning: A6 driver ALM asserted ALONE (no card servo-alarm status, no hard limit, no soft-limit) - a position/following-deviation alarm from the amp. Recovery per the name is re-home + restart. Classifier branch GetErrorIndex()==6 (MyMotor.cpp:746-747); csystem.cpp:500-501 also folds the never-returned iRef==9 into 6. code = 50000+index*10+6.
error_types.signal_source: Led[iAlarmLed]=MotDI 0x80 (A6 ALM) set while Led[iServoalarmLed], Led[iCwLed], Led[iCcwLed], Led[iSoftcwLed], Led[iSoftccwLed] are all OFF. A6 position/deviation (Err) alarm.
error_types.expected: ALM off; encoder tracks command (following error within tolerance); axis reaches and holds each target.
error_types.actual: Driver ALM latched from an excessive position/following deviation with no accompanying limit or card servo-alarm bit.
error_types.check_where: MotionView (command NowPos vs Encoder following gap) plus the Motor status grid (Alarm ON, all limit/servo-alarm LEDs OFF).
error_types.engineer_action: Re-HOME and restart the axis (per the alarm name). The latched amp alarm is not software-clearable, so power-cycle SwMotorRelay first, then re-HOME; investigate cause of the deviation (encoder coupling, gain, mechanical drag).

error_types.label: Undefine
error_types.meaning: Software fall-through of GetErrorIndex(): the Led[] snapshot matched none of the defined ALM/servo-alarm/limit/soft-limit patterns (MyMotor.cpp:750, the final 'return 7'). From the ScanAllMotorStatus path Led[iAlarmLed] is always true, so the 'else if(Led[iAlarmLed]) return 6' branch catches first and 7 is effectively unreachable there - it only surfaces on an inconsistent/transient status read. code = 50000+index*10+7.
error_types.signal_source: None - pure logic default of the classifier when no recognized status-bit combination is present (no dedicated IO). The logic variable is the returned errIndex itself.
error_types.expected: A genuine fault always matches a defined branch (0-6/8); errIndex 7 should not appear in normal operation.
error_types.actual: Status snapshot had no classifiable alarm bit -> transient/jittered MotDI+MotionInput read, or an alarm source not modeled by ScanMotorStatus.
error_types.check_where: State Record / EventLog (the raised 5xxx7 code and the surrounding Led snapshot) then re-read the Motor status grid live to see if it persists.
error_types.engineer_action: Re-scan the axis; if it recurs, capture the raw MotDI/MotionInput words (ReadStatus) - likely a status-word/wiring anomaly. Treat as an unclassified driver alarm and power-cycle + re-HOME.

error_types.label: Target will Out Of Limit
error_types.meaning: A commanded move target lies outside the soft-limit band, so the move is rejected BEFORE any motion. This is the primary runtime use: raised directly (not through GetErrorIndex) by the per-axis pre-move guard when CheckSoftLimit(target)==false. (The GetErrorIndex()==8 branch, MyMotor.cpp:748-749, only fires when iAlarmLed is off but the MotionInput servo-alarm bit is set - unreachable from the gated scan path.) Raised as AlarmName[eMotOverLimitErr] via ShowMotorLimitError; code = 50000+index*10+8.
error_types.signal_source: Logic/soft-limit compare, no IO bit: CheckSoftLimit(p) = (p<=SoftLimitP && p>=SoftLimitN) in MyMotor.cpp:503-507; sets bErrorMove in MotorMoveSub (MyMotor.cpp:523). Callers: aAuto1To6.cpp:370-373, aLoader.cpp:268/434, aEmpty.cpp:247, aColor.cpp:887/917/1168, aTrayArm.cpp:409, aSortArm.cpp:722/736/750.
error_types.expected: Requested target within [SoftLimitN, SoftLimitP]; CheckSoftLimit returns true and MotorMove proceeds.
error_types.actual: Requested target outside the soft-limit band -> CheckSoftLimit false, bErrorMove=true, move blocked; the Note prints SoftLimitDetail 'target=.. now=.. soft limit N=.. ~ P=.. (unit:1/100mm)' (MyMotor.cpp:512-516, note.cpp:865-871).
error_types.check_where: Note detail line (the printed SoftLimitDetail target/now/limit values, prefixed by the axis NumberAlias) plus MotionView (configured SoftLimitN/P vs the teach target).
error_types.engineer_action: Correct the teach position or the requested target so it falls inside [SoftLimitN, SoftLimitP], or fix the SoftLimitN/SoftLimitP configuration for that axis; re-HOME if the axis position reference is off (a lost datum can push a valid target out of band).

error_types.label: 60000  Suck--Pick Up Error (ShowSuckError CodeType 1, SUCxxx1)
error_types.meaning: Pick-up confirmation failed. TMySucker::Suck() drove vacuum ON (On() = OffDestroy()+OnSuck(), i.e. blow valve OffSw off, suck valve OnSw on) and waited OnAlarmTime for the vacuum sensor to confirm ON; it never came ON, so the IC was not sucked onto the nozzle.
error_types.expected: HEALTHY: after the suck command the vacuum sensor of the picking nozzle (TMySucker::Sensor, per-nozzle alias SuckAa/SuckAb/SuckAc/SuckAd = SuckerName Suck1..Suck4) reads ON within OnAlarmTime, so SensorAllOn()==true and Suck() advances Task 1->50->100 returning true.
error_types.actual: FAULT: vacuum sensor stays OFF past OnAlarmTime. Entry gate MyKitSuck.cpp:195 `if(Sensor.Enable==true && SensorAllOn()==false && HSys.LastSet.iRealDummy==REALLY)` sends Task=50; the OnAlarmTime timer expires with sensor still OFF at MyKitSuck.cpp:220-225 `else if(Delay.Off()){Error=true; OffSuck(); Task=1; return false;}`. aSortArm SuckSelectedSlots latches bPickSuckErr[slot] (aSortArm.cpp:1178-1183) and later raises ShowSuckError(*Sucker,1,...) at aSortArm.cpp:1741.
error_types.check_where: IOsetview — vacuum sensor LED of the failed nozzle (Suck.Sensor SuckAa..SuckAd). It should latch ON right after the Suck-Z presses down; on this fault the LED never lights.
error_types.engineer_action: Confirm an IC is actually present in the source tray cell (empty cell = expected no-pick). If IC present but sensor never lights: check air/vacuum supply pressure, check for a leak or clogged/worn nozzle tip and bad seal (IC tilted), and verify the suck solenoid OnSw fires (IOsetview output) and the vacuum-sensor wiring. Root causes: no IC / leak / clogged nozzle / low vacuum / sensor dead.

error_types.label: 60001  Suck--Destory Error (release; ShowSuckError CodeType 2 at place, SUCxxx2)
error_types.meaning: Release/destroy confirmation failed. TMySucker::Destroy() drove vacuum OFF + blow (Off() = OffSuck()+OnDestroy(), suck valve OnSw off, blow valve OffSw on) and waited OffAlarmTime for the vacuum sensor to drop OFF; the sensor stayed ON, so the IC did not release from the nozzle.
error_types.expected: HEALTHY: after the release command the vacuum sensor falls OFF within OffAlarmTime, so SensorAnyOn()==false and Destroy() advances Task 1->50->100 returning true (IC placed into the target cell).
error_types.actual: FAULT: vacuum sensor still reads ON past OffAlarmTime. Entry gate MyKitSuck.cpp:262 `if(Sensor.Enable==true && SensorAnyOn()==true && HSys.LastSet.iRealDummy==REALLY)` sends Task=50; the OffAlarmTime timer expires with sensor still ON at MyKitSuck.cpp:287-292 `else if(Delay.Off()){Error=true; OffDestroy(); Task=1; return false;}`. Raised via ShowSuckError(*Sucker,2,K_RETRY|K_SKIP,"SortArm Place") at aSortArm.cpp:1389.
error_types.check_where: IOsetview — vacuum sensor LED of the placing nozzle (Suck.Sensor SuckAa..SuckAd). It should extinguish when the blow fires; on this fault the LED stays lit.
error_types.engineer_action: Verify the blow/destroy valve OffSw actually fires and positive-pressure air is present (IOsetview output + air line). Check the IC is not physically stuck to the nozzle and the suck solenoid OnSw truly dropped. If the sensor is lit with no vacuum, suspect a stuck-ON or shorted vacuum sensor. Root causes: IC stuck (didn't release) / solenoid stuck ON / no blow air / sensor stuck ON.

error_types.label: 60002  Suck--Vacuum Sensor Off Error (lost vacuum while holding)
error_types.meaning: A nozzle that should be holding an IC lost its vacuum — the held-vacuum monitor read the vacuum sensor OFF while the slot is marked carrying (bHasIC). This is the vacuum-sensor-OFF primitive judged by TMySucker::GetStatus()/SensorAllOn().
error_types.expected: HEALTHY: while a SortArm slot carries an IC (Slot[s].bHasIC==true) the nozzle's vacuum sensor is held continuously ON, so GetStatusAllOn()==true (GetStatus REALLY-guard MyKitSuck.cpp:106-111 + SensorAllOn MyKitSuck.cpp:82-92).
error_types.actual: FAULT: vacuum sensor reads OFF mid-hold. The held re-read at aSortArm.cpp:1533 and :1565 `if(Sucker->GetStatusAllOn()==false)` trips. GetStatus() is Sensor.IsOn() on the real machine (MyKitSuck.cpp:72-77). A momentary/partial loss surfaces here before the debounce window escalates it to a confirmed drop (60003).
error_types.check_where: IOsetview — vacuum sensor LED of the holding nozzle (Suck.Sensor SuckAa..SuckAd). It should stay solid ON during transit; on this fault it flickers or drops OFF.
error_types.engineer_action: Inspect for a developing leak or marginal seal on that nozzle, air-pressure sag under load, a partially clogged tip, or an intermittent vacuum sensor / loose connector. Note: REALLY-only — never fires in SOFT_SIMULATE (GetStatus returns true when iRealDummy!=REALLY). Root causes: leak / marginal seal / clogged / intermittent sensor.

error_types.label: 60003  Suck--Device Be Droped Error (ShowSuckError CodeType 3, SUCxxx3)
error_types.meaning: A held IC physically dropped in transit. A holding nozzle's vacuum sensor read OFF and stayed OFF past the fall-down debounce window (FALLDOWN_LOST_MS) while the arm carried the IC from Loader toward Auto. The machine decel-stops all motion and the SortArm slot is written off (never counted as placed).
error_types.expected: HEALTHY: while carrying an IC the vacuum sensor is continuously ON; CheckIsFallDown() (MyKitSuck.cpp:327-333) sees Sensor.IsOn()==true and does nothing, and the module monitor CheckHoldFallDown never confirms an OFF.
error_types.actual: FAULT: vacuum sensor OFF persisting FALLDOWN_LOST_MS. Per-nozzle primitive MyKitSuck.cpp:331 `if(Sensor.IsOn()==false) Normal();` drops the outputs; the debounced module monitor CheckHoldFallDown (aSortArm.cpp:1526-1616) confirms via GetStatusAllOn()==false (:1533/:1565), calls HSys.StopAllMotor() (:1578), and raises ShowSuckError(*DropSucker,3,...) at aSortArm.cpp:1596. bAtPick decides whether the Loader source cell is restored (K_RETRY) or abandoned EMPTY_IC (K_SKIP).
error_types.check_where: IOsetview — vacuum sensor LED of the dropped nozzle (Suck.Sensor SuckAa..SuckAd), plus the Note detail line which prints the dropped cell identity ("SortArm IC Dropped At Pick/In Transit R.. C.. 2D=..").
error_types.engineer_action: Retrieve the dropped IC from the machine, then find why the seal failed completely: sudden vacuum loss, worn/cracked nozzle, IC snagged during travel, or vacuum-pressure collapse. Distinguished from 60002 only by the debounced, motion-halting confirmation. Root cause: dropped (seal broke) / abrupt vacuum loss.

error_types.label: 60004  Suck--Initial Sensor Off Error (registered taxonomy; no active runtime raise)
error_types.meaning: Initial-state sensor self-check taxonomy: at init/reset with vacuum energized the nozzle's vacuum sensor should confirm ON; a stuck-OFF sensor or dead vacuum path would be this code. IMPORTANT — this is a REGISTERED taxonomy code only: the init self-check TMyKitSuck::CheckVaccumIsIniaialON (MyKitSuck.cpp:657-677) has no caller anywhere in HT160S, and no runtime site raises eSuckIniOffErr. On the live machine the same 'vacuum won't turn ON' condition surfaces instead as eSuckPickErr (60000).
error_types.expected: HEALTHY (intended semantic): with vacuum commanded ON at initialization the vacuum sensor reads ON (GetStatus()==true).
error_types.actual: FAULT (intended semantic): vacuum sensor stays OFF when vacuum is energized. No live if() raises this in HT160S; it exists in mapAlarmCodeList / AlarmList.csv (database.cpp:911,898) as Name+"_SuckIniOffErr" for the taxonomy.
error_types.check_where: IOsetview — vacuum sensor LED of the nozzle (Suck.Sensor SuckAa..SuckAd); it would fail to light when vacuum is applied at init.
error_types.engineer_action: Treat as documentation/taxonomy: if seen it originates from the sensor never asserting ON — check dead vacuum generator, no air supply, disconnected/stuck-OFF sensor, wiring. In practice diagnose the live pick fault 60000 with the same checks. State-wise verify in State Record / EventLog that the code is a registered entry, not a fired event.

error_types.label: 60005  Suck--Initial Sensor On Error (residue/stuck-ON at init; registered taxonomy)
error_types.meaning: At power-up/reset/init a nozzle with NO IC assigned should hold no vacuum (sensor OFF); instead the vacuum sensor reads ON. The intended logic lives in TMyKitSuck::CheckVaccumIsIniaialON (MyKitSuck.cpp:657-677): if GetStatus()==true (:662) while Item is a Null/empty type (:664-667) it forces Normal() and sets Flag=true (:669-670). IMPORTANT — CheckVaccumIsIniaialON has no active caller in HT160S; 60005 is a registered taxonomy code (AlarmList.csv), not raised at runtime.
error_types.expected: HEALTHY: at idle/init with no IC assigned (Item==SuckNullIC/SuckHasNullIC/test variants) the vacuum sensor reads OFF, so GetStatus()==false and CheckVaccumIsIniaialON takes the else branch (:673-675) calling Normal() with no flag.
error_types.actual: FAULT (intended semantic): vacuum sensor reads ON at init on an empty nozzle. CheckVaccumIsIniaialON GetStatus()==true with an empty Item -> Normal()+Flag=true (MyKitSuck.cpp:662-671). Because the function is not wired in, no live if() raises the code today.
error_types.check_where: IOsetview — vacuum sensor LED of the nozzle (Suck.Sensor SuckAa..SuckAd); on this condition the LED is lit at startup with no IC held.
error_types.engineer_action: If the vacuum sensor is lit at init with nothing picked, check for a vacuum solenoid stuck ON / mis-wired (NC) OnSw, a stuck or shorted vacuum sensor, or a stray IC still adhered from the previous cycle. Root causes: stuck-ON valve / sensor stuck ON / residue IC. Confirm in State Record / EventLog whether 60005 is merely the registered taxonomy entry versus an actual fired event.
